summary: Completed Module 3 reflection with evidence-backed conclusions: synthetic reproduction isolated concurrency races, fixes were validated under matched workloads, and silent timestamp deltas were correctly interpreted as DB write-time semantics after regression-proofing with GREATEST.
evidence: Decision callback (Choice B: synthetic reproduction): Kept the same controlled concurrent workloads before and after fixes, which enabled clean causal verification of both failure reproduction and elimination.

Hypothesis-driven elimination: proved concurrency was the trigger by reproducing 500 + UniqueViolation under concurrent load, while ruling out data/timing-only explanations with matched inputs and post-fix controls.
Root cause #1: check-then-act race in analytics writes caused duplicate-key failures under overlap; fixed with atomic ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.

Root cause #2: silent timestamp semantics under concurrent upserts required monotonic timestamp protection; fixed with last_accessed_at = GREATEST(analytics.last_accessed_at, EXCLUDED.last_accessed_at).
Verification proof: no 500 responses under fixed workload, no timestamp regression across rounds, monotonic last_accessed_at behavior, and exact +10 count increments per 10-request round.
Residual timestamp gap interpretation: differences between DB last_accessed_at and latest HTTP completion are expected DB write-time semantics, not silent corruption.
